prompt: Design a service that lets neighbours lend physical books. Prevent two borrowers reserving the same copy; support waiting lists, late returns, and unreliable notifications.
provenance: Original synthetic answer authored for mockr; not an actual candidate or human-scored label.

transcript.answer: Reserve individual copies, not titles. Limit to one active borrower per copy and prioritize correct reservations over stale search. Notifications are asynchronous.
Assume 20000 users with two reads per day and 2000 daily writes. Average read load is 0.46 requests per second; a 20x peak is under ten per second.
POST /copies/{id}/reservations accepts an idempotency key and returns a reservation or conflict. GET /reservations/{id} returns status. Errors distinguish unavailable copies and invalid users.
Copy has copy_id and title_id. Reservation has id, copy_id, borrower_id and status. A partial unique index prevents multiple active reservations per copy.
Use a transactional outbox for notifications. Retries are idempotent. Monitor conflicts, queue age and delivery failures. Start with one database and add replicas for catalog reads.
Strong writes cost availability during database failover. Stale catalog reads are acceptable but a reservation must recheck the primary. I would not shard before measuring a bottleneck.
